# `show`

How an event appears when it is played back: changes to the picture, an animation, a log line, what to do if it was only heard (12 §7.3).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `on` (string; **required**): The event this is about, by its registered name.
- `filter` (object, name → [`Literal`](#literal); optional): A cheap test on the event's plain fields: each named field must hold the constant given (05 §8.4).
- `if` ([condition](../values.md#conditions), or `null`; optional): `if`: a condition in the event's scope. The show applies only while it holds.
- `change` (list of [`ChangeDef`](#changedef), or `null`; optional): The changes to the picture of the world, made when the event was seen. Left out, everything the event is about is observed again; an empty list changes nothing.
- `anim` (string, or `null`; optional): The animation played, by the id of an `anim` definition.
- `at` (string, or `null`; optional): The subject the animation plays at. Left out, `here`.
- `to` (string, or `null`; optional): The subject a travelling animation ends at.
- `log` ([text](../values.md#texts), or `null`; optional): The line written to the log, a template in the event's scope worded for the reader (05 §4.6).
- `category` (string, or `null`; optional): The category of its lines, which a `log` widget filters by. Left out, `event`.
- `heard` (object [`HeardDef`](#hearddef), or `null`; optional): What to do if the event was only heard.
- `shake` (number; optional): Screen shake as the event is played, from 0 to 1, dying away over `time`.
- `flash` (string, or `null`; optional): A colour flashed over the whole frame, dying away over `time`.
- `time` ([time](../units.md#time) in `s`, or `null`; optional): How long the show's own effects last: the glide of a sprite it moves, its shake and its flash. Left out, 150 ms.
- `min_time` ([time](../units.md#time) in `s`, or `null`; optional): How long the event holds the queue: nothing later is played before this has passed.
- `importance` (one of `"minor"`, `"normal"`, `"major"` ([`Importance`](#importance)); optional): How much the event matters: `minor`, `normal` or `major`.
- `sound` (string, or `null`; optional): The name of a sound cue. It is handed on with the event and nothing plays it yet.

<a id="literal"></a>
### `Literal`

A literal value in a definition: `true`, `3`, `0.5` or `"text"`.

Written as true, false, a number or a text.

Takes:

- a string
- an integer
- a number
- a boolean

<a id="changedef"></a>
### `ChangeDef`

One change a `show` makes to the picture of the world when its event was seen (12 §7.3): an object with one key.

One of:

- `{ "cell": … }` with string: `{ "cell": "here" }`: the cell a subject names is observed again: what the party sees there replaces what was known of it.
- `{ "field": … }` with string: `{ "field": "here" }`: only the strongest field of the cell a subject names is taken from what the party sees there.
- `{ "sprite": … }` with [`SpriteChangeDef`](#spritechangedef): `{ "sprite": "self" }` or `{ "sprite": { "of": "self", "to": "here" } }`: the perceived thing a subject names moved, appeared or changed.
- `{ "gone": … }` with string: `{ "gone": "self" }`: the sprite of the thing a subject names is removed.

<a id="hearddef"></a>
### `HeardDef`

What a `show` does when its event was only heard (12 §5): a marker where it seemed to come from, and a log line. Never a picture.

- `log` ([text](../values.md#texts), or `null`; optional): The line written to the log, a template in the event's scope.
- `marker` (one character, or `null`; optional): The character the marker is drawn with. Left out, the theme's `heard` mark.

<a id="importance"></a>
### `Importance`

How much a line, or the showing of an event, matters (12 §7.3). A `log` widget may show only lines of at least some importance, and the preference `effects` may play only the animations of what is `major`.

One of:

- `"minor"`: Detail: a step, a door, a scuff.
- `"normal"`: What a player would want to have read.
- `"major"`: What must not be missed.

<a id="spritechangedef"></a>
### `SpriteChangeDef`

The `sprite` change: which thing, and where it now is.

Written as a subject's name, or an object with `of` and `to`.

Takes:

- a string
- an object: object [`SpriteChangeObject`](#spritechangeobject)

<a id="spritechangeobject"></a>
### `SpriteChangeObject`

The object form of `SpriteChangeDef`.

- `of` (string; **required**): The subject of the event that names the thing whose sprite changes.
- `to` (string, or `null`; optional): The subject that names the cell it is in now. Left out, or not bound by the event, it is where the party perceives it.
